1.1: And it comes to pass, after the death of Saul, that David has returned from smiting the Amalekite, and David dwells in Ziklag two days,
1.2: and it comes to pass, on the third day, that indeed, a man has come in out of the camp from Saul, and his garments are rent, and earth on his head; and it comes to pass, in his coming in to David, that he falls to the earth, and does obeisance.
1.3: And David says to him, `From where do you come?' and he says to him, `Out of the camp of Israel I have escaped.'
1.4: And David says to him, `What has been the matter? declare, I pray you, to me.' And he says, that `The people has fled from the battle, and also a multitude has fallen of the people, and they die; and also Saul and Jonathan his son have died.'
1.5: And David says to the youth who is declaring it to him, `How have you known that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?'
1.6: And the youth who is declaring it to him says, I happened to meet in mount Gilboa, and indeed, Saul is leaning on his spear; and indeed, the chariots and those possessing horses have followed him;
1.7: and he turns behind him, and sees me, and calls to me, and I say, Here am I.
1.8: And he says to me, Who are you? and I say to him, An Amalekite I am.'
1.9: `And he says to me, Stand, I pray you, over me, and put me to death, for seized me has the arrow, for all my soul is still in me.
1.10: And I stand over him, and put him to death, for I knew that he does not live after his falling, and I take the crown which is on his head, and the bracelet which is on his arm, and bring them in to my lord here.'
1.11: And David takes hold on his garments, and rends them, and also all the men who are with him,
1.12: and they mourn, and weep, and fast till the evening, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel, because they have fallen by the sword.
1.13: And David says to the youth who is declaring it to him, `From where are you?' and he says, `Son of a sojourner, an Amalekite, I am.'
1.14: And David says to him, `How were you not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the anointed of Jehovah?'
1.15: And David calls to one of the youths, and says, `Draw nigh--fall upon him;' and he smites him, and he dies;
1.16: and David says to him, `Your blood is on your own head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, I--I put to death the anointed of Jehovah.'
1.17: And David laments with this lamentation over Saul, and over Jonathan his son;
1.18: and he says to teach the sons of Judah `The Bow;' indeed, it is written on the book of the Upright: --
1.19: `The Roebuck, O Israel, On your high places is wounded; How have the mighty fallen!
1.20: Declare it not in Gath, Proclaim not the tidings in the streets of Ashkelon, Lest they rejoice--The daughters of the Philistines, Lest they exult--The daughters of the Uncircumcised!
1.21: Mountains of Gilboa! No dew nor rain be on you, And fields of heave-offerings! For there has become loathsome The shield of the mighty, The shield of Saul--without the anointed with oil.
1.22: From the blood of the wounded, From the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan Has not turned backward; And the sword of Saul does not return empty.
1.23: Saul and Jonathan! They are loved and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they have not been parted. Than eagles they have been lighter, Than lions they have been mightier!
1.24: Daughters of Israel! for Saul weep you, Who is clothing you in scarlet with delights. Who is lifting up ornaments of gold on your clothing.
1.25: How have the mighty fallen In the midst of the battle! Jonathan! on your high places wounded!
1.26: I am in distress for you, my brother Jonathan, Very pleasant were you to me; Wonderful was your love to me, Above the love of women!
1.27: How have the mighty fallen, Yes, the weapons of war perish!'

2.1: And it comes to pass afterwards, that David asks at Jehovah, saying, `Do I go up into one of the cities of Judah?' and Jehovah says to him, `Go up.' And David says, `Where do I go up?' and He says, `To Hebron.'
2.2: And David goes up there, and also his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite;
2.3: and his men who are with him has David brought up--a man and his household--and they dwell in the cities of Hebron.
2.4: And the men of Judah come, and anoint there David for king over the house of Judah; and they declare to David, saying, `The men of Jabesh-Gilead are they who buried Saul.'
2.5: And David sends messengers to the men of Jabesh-Gilead, and says to them, `Blessed are you of Jehovah, in that you have done this kindness with your lord, with Saul, that you bury him.
2.6: `And, now, Jehovah does with you kindness and truth, and also, I do with you this good because you have done this thing;
2.7: and now, are your hands strong, and be you for sons of valour, for your lord Saul. is dead, and also--me have the house of Judah anointed for king over them.'
2.8: And Abner, son of Ner, head of the host which Saul has, has taken Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, and causes him to pass over to Mahanaim,
2.9: and causes him to reign over Gilead, and over the Ashurite, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over Israel--all of it.
2.10: A son of forty years, is Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, in his reigning over Israel, and two years he has reigned, only the house of Judah have been after David.
2.11: And the number of the days that David has been king in Hebron, over the house of Judah, is seven years and six months.
2.12: And Abner son of Ner goes out, and servants of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
2.13: And Joab son of Zeruiah, and servants of David, have gone out, and they meet by the pool of Gibeon together, and sit down, these by the pool on this side, and these by the pool on that.
2.14: And Abner says to Joab, `Let the youths rise, I pray you, and they play before us;' and Joab says, `Let them rise.'
2.15: And they rise and pass over, in number twelve of Benjamin, even of Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
2.16: And they lay hold, each on the head of his companion, and his sword is in the side of his companion, and they fall together, and one calls that place Helkath-Hazzurim, which is in Gibeon,
2.17: and the battle is very hard on that day, and Abner is smitten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
2.18: And there are there three sons of Zeruiah, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel, and Asahel is light on his feet, as one of the roes which are in the field,
2.19: And Asahel pursues after Abner, and has not turned aside to go to the right or to the left, from after Abner.
2.20: And Abner looks behind him, and says, `Are you he--Asahel?' and he says, `I am.'
2.21: And Abner says to him, `Turn you aside to your right hand or to your left, and seize for you one of the youths, and take to you his armour;' and Asahel has not been willing to turn aside from after him.
2.22: And Abner adds again, saying to Asahel, `Turn you aside from after me, why do I smite you to the earth? and how do I lift up my face to Joab your brother?'
2.23: And he refuses to turn aside, and Abner smites him with the hinder part of the spear to the fifth rib, and the spear comes out from behind him, and he falls there, and dies under it; and it comes to pass, every one who has come to the place where Asahel has fallen and dies--they stand still.
2.24: And Joab and Abishai pursue after Abner, and the sun has gone in, and they have come in to the height of Ammah, which is on the front of Giah, the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
2.25: And the sons of Benjamin gather themselves together after Abner, and become one troop, and stand on the top of a certain height,
2.26: and Abner calls to Joab, and says, `For ever does the sword consume? have you not known that it is bitterness in the latter end? and till when do you not say to the people to turn back from after their brethren?'
2.27: And Joab says, `God lives! for unless you had spoken, surely then from the morning had the people gone up each from after his brother.'
2.28: And Joab blows with a trumpet, and all the people stand still, and pursue no more after Israel, nor have they added any more to fight.
2.29: And Abner and his men have gone through the plain all that night, and pass over the Jordan, and go on through all Bithron, and come in to Mahanaim.
2.30: And Joab has turned back from after Abner, and gathers all the people, and there are lacking of the servants of David nineteen men, and Asahel;
2.31: and the servants of David have smitten of Benjamin, even among the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men--they died.
2.32: And they lift up Asahel, and bury him in the burying-place of his father, which is in Beth-Lehem, and they go all the night--Joab and his men--and it is light to them in Hebron.

3.1: And the war is long between the house of Saul and the house of David, and David is going on and is strong, and the house of Saul are going on and are weak.
3.2: And there are born to David sons in Hebron, and his first-born is Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess,
3.3: and his second is Chileab, of Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite, and the third is Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur,
3.4: and the fourth is Adonijah son of Haggith, and the fifth is Shephatiah son of Abital,
3.5: and the sixth is Ithream, of Eglah wife of David; these have been born to David in Hebron.
3.6: And it comes to pass, in the war being between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner has been strengthening himself in the house of Saul,
3.7: and Saul has a concubine, and her name is Rizpah daughter of Aiah, and Ish-Bosheth says to Abner, `Wherefore have you gone in to the concubine of my father?'
3.8: And it is displeasing to Abner exceedingly, because of the words of Ish-Bosheth, and he says, `The head of a dog am I--that in reference to Judah to-day I do kindness with the house of Saul your father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David--that you charge against me iniquity concerning the woman to-day?
3.9: thus does God to Abner, and thus He does add to him, surely as Jehovah has sworn to David--surely so I do to him:
3.10: to cause the kingdom to pass over from the house of Saul, and to raise up the throne of David over Israel, and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-Sheba.'
3.11: And he is not able any more to turn back Abner a word, because of his fearing him.
3.12: And Abner sends messengers to David for himself, saying, `Whose is the land?' saying, `Make your covenant with me, and indeed, my hand is with you, to bring round to you all Israel.'
3.13: And he says, `Good--I make with you a covenant; only, one thing I am asking of you, that is, You do not see my face, except you do first bring in Michal, daughter of Saul in your coming into see my face.'
3.14: And David sends messengers to Ish-Bosheth son of Saul, saying, `Give up my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself with a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.'
3.15: And Ish-Bosheth sends, and takes her from a man, from Phaltiel son of Laish,
3.16: and her husband goes with her, going on and weeping behind her, to Bahurim, and Abner says to him, `Go, turn back;' and he turns back.
3.17: And the word of Abner was with the elders of Israel, saying, `Heretofore you have been seeking David for king over you,
3.18: and now, do it, for Jehovah has spoken of David saying, By the hand of David my servant--to save My people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.'
3.19: And Abner speaks also in the ears of Benjamin, and Abner goes also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that is good in the eyes of Israel, and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin,
3.20: and Abner comes in to David, to Hebron, and with him twenty men, and David makes for Abner, and for the men who are with him, a banquet.
3.21: And Abner says to David, `I arise, and go, and gather to my lord the king the whole of Israel, and they make with you a covenant, and you have reigned over all that your soul desires;' and David sends away Abner, and he goes in peace.
3.22: And indeed, the servants of David, and Joab, have come from the troop, and much spoil have brought with them, and Abner is not with David in Hebron, for he has sent him away, and he goes in peace;
3.23: and Joab and all the host that is with him have come, and they declare to Joab, saying, `Abner son of Ner has come to the king, and he sends him away, and he goes in peace.'
3.24: And Joab comes to the king, and says, `What have you done? indeed, Abner has come to you! why is this--you have sent him away, and he is really gone?
3.25: You have known Abner son of Ner, that to deceive you he came, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you are doing.'
3.26: And Joab goes out from David, and sends messengers after Abner, and they bring him back from the well of Sirah, and David knew not.
3.27: And Abner turns back to Hebron, and Joab turns him aside to the midst of the gate to speak with him quietly, and smites him there in the fifth rib --and he dies--for the blood of Asahel his brother.
3.28: And David hears afterwards and says, `Acquitted am I, and my kingdom, by Jehovah, to the age, from the blood of Abner son of Ner;
3.29: it does stay on the head of Joab, and on all the house of his father, and there is not cut off from the house of Joab one having an issue, and leprous, and laying hold on a staff, and falling by a sword, and lacking bread.'
3.30: And Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner because that he put to death Asahel their brother, in Gibeon, in battle.
3.31: And David says to Joab, and to all the people who are with him, `Rend your garments, and gird on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner;' and king David is going after the bier.
3.32: And they bury Abner in Hebron, and the king lifts up his voice, and weeps at the grave of Abner, and all the people weep;
3.33: and the king laments for Abner, and says: --`As the death of a fool does Abner die?
3.34: Your hands not bound, And your feet to fetters not brought nigh! As one falling before sons of evil--You have fallen!' and all the people add to weep over him.
3.35: And all the people come to cause David to eat bread while yet day, and David swears, saying, `Thus does God to me, and thus He does add, for--before the going in of the sun, I taste no bread or any other thing.'
3.36: And all the people have discerned it, and it is good in their eyes, as all that the king has done is good in the eyes of all the people;
3.37: and all the people know, even all Israel, in that day, that it has not been from the king--to put to death Abner son of Ner.
3.38: And the king says to his servants, `Do you not know that a prince and a great one has fallen this day in Israel?
3.39: and I to-day am tender, and an anointed king: and these men, sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me; Jehovah does recompense to the doer of the evil according to his evil.'

4.1: And the son of Saul hears that Abner is dead in Hebron, and his hands are feeble, and all Israel have been troubled.
4.2: And two men, heads of troops, have been to the son of Saul, the name of the one is Baanah, and the name of the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin, for also Beeroth is reckoned to Benjamin,
4.3: and the Beerothites flee to Gittaim, and are there sojourners to this day.
4.4: And to Jonathan son of Saul is a son--lame; he was a son of five years at the coming in of the rumour of the death of Saul and Jonathan, out of Jezreel, and his nurse lifts him up, and flees, and it comes to pass in her hasting to flee, that he falls, and becomes lame, and his name is Mephibosheth.
4.5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, go, and come in at the heat of the day to the house of Ish-Bosheth, and he is lying down--the lying down of noon;
4.6: and there they have come, to the midst of the house, taking wheat, and they smite him to the fifth rib, and Rechab and Baanah his brother have escaped;
4.7: yes, they come in to the house, and he is lying on his bed, in the inner part of his bed-chamber, and they smite him, and put him to death, and turn aside his head, and they take his head, and go the way of the plain all the night,
4.8: and bring in the head of Ish-Bosheth to David in Hebron, and say to the king, `Indeed, the head of Ish-Bosheth, son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life; and Jehovah does give to my lord the king vengeance this day, of Saul and of his seed.'
4.9: And David answers Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and says to them, `Jehovah lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
4.10: when one is declaring to me, saying, Indeed, Saul is dead, and he was as a bearer of tidings in his own eyes, then I take hold on him, and slay him in Ziklag, instead of my giving to him for the tidings.
4.11: Also--when wicked men have slain the righteous man in his own house, on his bed; and now, do not I require his blood of your hand, and have taken you away from the earth?'
4.12: And David commands the young men, and they slay them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hang them over the pool in Hebron, and the head of Ish-Bosheth they have taken, and bury it in the burying-place of Abner in Hebron.

5.1: And all the tribes of Israel come to David, to Hebron, and speak, saying, `Indeed, we are your bone and your flesh;
5.2: also heretofore, in Saul's being king over us, you have been he who is bringing out and bringing in Israel, and Jehovah says to you, You do feed My people Israel, and you are for leader over Israel.'
5.3: And all the elders of Israel come to the king, to Hebron, and king David makes with them a covenant in Hebron before Jehovah, and they anoint David for king over Israel.
5.4: A son of thirty years is David in his being king; forty years he has reigned;
5.5: in Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years, over all Israel and Judah.
5.6: And the king goes, and his men, to Jerusalem, to the Jebusite, the inhabitant of the land, and they speak to David, saying, `You do not come in here, except you turn aside the blind and the lame;' saying, `David does not come in here.'
5.7: And David captures the fortress of Zion, it is the city of David.
5.8: And David says on that day, `Any one smiting the Jebusite, (let him go up by the watercourse), and the lame and the blind--the hated of David's soul,' --because the blind and lame say, `He does not come into the house.'
5.9: And David dwells in the fortress, and calls it--City of David, and David builds round about, from Millo and inward,
5.10: and David goes, going on and becoming great, and Jehovah, God of Hosts, is with him.
5.11: And Hiram king of Tyre sends messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and artificers of wood, and artificers of stone, for walls, and they build a house for David,
5.12: and David knows that Jehovah has established him for king over Israel, and that He has lifted up his kingdom, because of His people Israel.
5.13: And David takes again concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after his coming from Hebron, and there are born again to David sons and daughters.
5.14: And these are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
5.15: and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
5.16: and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
5.17: And the Philistines hear that they have anointed David for king over Israel, and all the Philistines come up to seek David, and David hears, and goes down to the fortress,
5.18: and the Philistines have come, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
5.19: And David asks of Jehovah, saying, `Do I go up to the Philistines? do You give them into my hand?' And Jehovah says to David, `Go up, for I certainly give the Philistines into your hand.'
5.20: And David comes in to Baal-Perazim, and David smites them there, and says, `Jehovah has broken forth on my enemies before me, as the breaking forth of waters;' therefore he has called the name of that place Baal-Perazim.
5.21: And they forsake there their idols, and David and his men lift them up.
5.22: And the Philistines add again to come up, and are spread out in the valley of Rephaim,
5.23: and David asks of Jehovah, and He says, `You do not go up, turn round to their rear, and you have come to them over-against the mulberries,
5.24: and it comes to pass, in your hearing the sound of a stepping in the tops of the mulberries, then you do move sharply, for then has Jehovah gone out before you to smite in the camp of the Philistines.'
5.25: And David does so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smites the Philistines from Geba to your coming to Gazer.

6.1: And David gathered again every chosen one in Israel, thirty thousand,
6.2: and David rises and goes, and all the people who are with him, from Baale-Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, whose name has been called--the name of Jehovah of Hosts, inhabiting the cherubs--upon it.
6.3: And they cause the ark of God to ride on a new cart, and lift it up from the house of Abinadab, which is in the height, and Uzzah and Ahio sons of Abinadab are leading the new cart;
6.4: and they lift it up from the house of Abinadab, which is in the height, with the ark of God, and Ahio is going before the ark,
6.5: and David and all the house of Israel are playing before Jehovah, with all kinds of instruments of fir-wood, even with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with cornets, and with cymbals.
6.6: And they come to the threshing-floor of Nachon, and Uzzah puts forth his hand to the ark of God, and lays hold on it, for they released the oxen;
6.7: and the anger of Jehovah burns against Uzzah, and God smites him there for the error, and he dies there by the ark of God.
6.8: And it is displeasing to David, because that Jehovah has broken forth a breach upon Uzzah, and one calls that place Perez-Uzzah, to this day;
6.9: and David fears Jehovah on that day, and says, `How does the ark of Jehovah come in to me?'
6.10: And David has not been willing to turn aside to himself the ark of Jehovah, to the city of David, and David turns it aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite,
6.11: and the ark of Jehovah does inhabit the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and Jehovah blesses Obed-Edom and all his house.
6.12: And it is declared to king David, saying, `Jehovah has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that he has, because of the ark of God;' and David goes and brings up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom to the city of David with joy.
6.13: And it comes to pass, when those bearing the ark of Jehovah have stepped six steps, that he sacrifices an ox and a fatling.
6.14: And David is dancing with all strength before Jehovah, and David is girded with a linen ephod,
6.15: and David and all the house of Israel are bringing up the ark of Jehovah with shouting, and with the voice of a trumpet,
6.16: and it has come to pass, the ark of Jehovah has come in to the city of David, and Michal daughter of Saul, has looked through the window, and sees king David moving and dancing before Jehovah, and despises him in her heart.
6.17: And they bring in the ark of Jehovah, and set it up in its place, in the midst of the tent which David has spread out for it, and David causes to ascend burnt-offerings before Jehovah, and peace-offerings.
6.18: And David finishes from causing to ascend the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings, and blesses the people in the name of Jehovah of Hosts,
6.19: and he apportions to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, from man even to woman, to each, one cake of bread, and one eshpar, and one ashisha, and all the people go, each to his house.
6.20: And David turns back to bless his house, and Michal daughter of Saul goes out to meet David, and says, `How honourable to-day was the king of Israel, who was uncovered to-day before the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain ones is openly uncovered!'
6.21: And David says to Michal, `--Before Jehovah, who fixed on me above your father, and above all his house, to appoint me leader over the people of Jehovah, and over Israel, --yes, I played before Jehovah;
6.22: and I have been more vile than this, and have been low in my eyes, and with the handmaids whom you have spoken of, with them I am honoured.'
6.23: As to Michal daughter of Saul, she had no child till the day of her death.

7.1: And it comes to pass, when the king sat in his house, and Jehovah has given rest to him round about, from all his enemies,
7.2: that the king says to Nathan the prophet, `See, I pray you, I am dwelling in a house of cedars, and the ark of God is dwelling in the midst of the curtain.'
7.3: And Nathan says to the king, `All that is in your heart--go, do, for Jehovah is with you.'
7.4: And it comes to pass in that night, that the word of Jehovah is to Nathan, saying,
7.5: `Go, and you have said to My servant, to David, Thus said Jehovah, Do you build for Me a house for My dwelling in?
7.6: for I have not dwelt in a house even from the day of My bringing up the sons of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, and am walking up and down in a tent and in a tabernacle.
7.7: During all the time that I have walked up and down among all the sons of Israel, a word have I spoken with one of the tribes of Israel which I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, `Why have you not built to Me a house of cedars?
7.8: and now, thus do you say to My servant, to David: `Thus said Jehovah of Hosts, I have taken you from the comely place, from after the flock, to be leader over My people, over Israel;
7.9: and I am with you wherever you have gone, and I cut off all your enemies from your presence, and have made for you a great name, as the name of the great ones who are in the earth,
7.10: and I have appointed a place for My people, for Israel, and have planted it, and it has tabernacled in its place, and it is not troubled any more, and the sons of perverseness do not add to afflict it any more, as in the beginning,
7.11: even from the day that I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I have given rest to you from all your enemies, and Jehovah has declared to you that Jehovah does make for you a house.
7.12: `When your days are full, and you have lain with your fathers, then I have raised up your seed after you which goes out from your bowels, and have established his kingdom;
7.13: He does build a house for My Name, and I have established the throne of his kingdom to the age.
7.14: I am to him for a father, and he is to Me for a son; whom in his dealings perversely I have even reproved with a rod of men, and with strokes of the sons of Adam,
7.15: and My kindness does not turn aside from him, as I turned it aside from Saul, whom I turned aside from before you,
7.16: and stedfast is your house and your kingdom to the age before you, your throne is established to the age.'
7.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spoke Nathan to David.
7.18: And king David comes in and sits before Jehovah, and says, `Who am I, Lord Jehovah? and what my house, that You have brought me hitherto?
7.19: And yet this is little in Your eyes, Lord Jehovah, and You do speak also concerning the house of Your servant afar off; and this is the law of the Man, Lord Jehovah.
7.20: And what does David add more to speak to You? and You, You have known Your servant, Lord Jehovah.
7.21: Because of Your word, and according to Your heart, You have done all this greatness, to cause Your servant to know it.
7.22: Therefore You have been great, Jehovah God, for there is none like You, and there is no God save You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
7.23: `And who is as Your people, as Israel--one nation in the earth, whom God has gone to redeem to Him for a people, and to make for Him a name--and to do for you the greatness--even fearful things for Your land, at the presence of Your people, whom You have redeemed to You out of Egypt-- among the nations and their gods?
7.24: Yes, You do establish to You Your people Israel, to You for a people to the age, and You, Jehovah, have been to them for God.
7.25: `And now, Jehovah God, the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant, and concerning his house, establish to the age, and do as You have spoken;
7.26: And Your Name is great to the age, saying, Jehovah of Hosts is God over Israel, and the house of Your servant David is established before You,
7.27: For You, Jehovah of Hosts, God of Israel, You have uncovered the ear of Your servant, saying, A house I build for you, therefore has Your servant found his heart to pray to You this prayer;
7.28: And now, Lord Jehovah, You are God Himself, and Your words are truth, and You speak to Your servant this goodness,
7.29: And now, begin and bless the house of Your servant, to be to the age before You, for You, Lord Jehovah, have spoken, and by Your blessing is the house of Your servant blessed--to the age.'

8.1: And it comes to pass afterwards that David smites the Philistines, and humbles them, and David takes the bridle of the metropolis out of the hand of the Philistines.
8.2: And he smites Moab, and measures them with a line, causing them to lie down on the earth, and he measures two lines to put to death, and the fulness of the line to keep alive, and the Moabites are to David for servants, bearers of a present.
8.3: And David smites Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, in his going to bring back his power by the River Euphrates;
8.4: and David captures from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen, and David destroys utterly the whole of the charioteers, only he leaves of them a hundred charioteers.
8.5: And Aram of Damascus comes to give help to Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David smites of Aram twenty and two thousand men;
8.6: and David puts garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram is to David for a servant, bearing a present; and Jehovah saves David wherever he has gone;
8.7: and David takes the shields of gold which were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brings them to Jerusalem;
8.8: and from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, has king David taken very much brass.
8.9: And Toi king of Hamath hears that David has smitten all the force of Hadadezer,
8.10: and Toi sends Joram his son to king David to ask of him of welfare, and to bless him, (because that he has fought against Hadadezer, and smites him, for a man of wars with Toi had Hadadezer been), and in his hand have been vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass,
8.11: also them did king David sanctify to Jehovah, with the silver and the gold which he sanctified of all the nations which he subdued:
8.12: of Aram, and of Moab, and of the Bene-Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah.
8.13: And David makes a name in his turning back from his smiting Aram in the valley of Salt--eighteen thousand;
8.14: and he puts in Edom garrisons--in all Edom he has put garrisons, and all Edom are servants to David; and Jehovah saves David wherever he has gone.
8.15: And David reigns over all Israel, and David is doing judgment and righteousness to all his people,
8.16: and Joab son of Zeruiah is over the host, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud is remembrancer,
8.17: and Zadok son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech son of Abiathar, are priests, and Seraiah is scribe,
8.18: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada is over both the Cherethite and the Pelethite, and the sons of David have been ministers.

9.1: And David says, `Is there yet any left to the house of Saul, and I do with him kindness because of Jonathan?'
9.2: And the house of Saul has a servant, and his name is Ziba, and they call for him to David; and the king says to him, `Are you Ziba?' and he says, `Your servant.'
9.3: And the king says, `Is there not yet a man to the house of Saul, and I do with him the kindness of God?' And Ziba says to the king, `Jonathan has yet a son--lame.'
9.4: And the king says to him, `Where is he?' and Ziba says to the king, `Indeed, he is in the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, in Indeed-Debar.'
9.5: And king David sends, and takes him out of the house of Machir son of Ammiel, of Indeed-Debar,
9.6: and Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, comes to David, and falls on his face, and does obeisance, and David says, `Mephibosheth;' and he says, `Indeed, your servant.'
9.7: And David says to him, `Be not afraid; for I certainly do with you kindness because of Jonathan your father, and have given back to you all the field of Saul your father, and you do eat bread at my table continually.'
9.8: And he bows himself, and says, `What is your servant, that you have turned to the dead dog--such as I?'
9.9: And the king calls to Ziba servant of Saul, and says to him, `All that was to Saul and to all his house, I have given to the son of your lord,
9.10: and you have served for him the land, you and your sons, and your servants, and have brought in, and there has been to the son of your lord bread, and he has eaten it; and Mephibosheth son of your lord does eat continually bread at my table;' and Ziba has fifteen sons and twenty servants.
9.11: And Ziba says to the king, `According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so does your servant;' as to Mephibosheth, `he is eating at my table (says the king) as one of the sons of the king.'
9.12: And Mephibosheth has a young son, and his name is Micha, and every one dwelling in the house of Ziba are servants to Mephibosheth.
9.13: And Mephibosheth is dwelling in Jerusalem, for at the table of the king he is eating continually, and he is lame of his two feet.

10.1: And it comes to pass afterwards, that the king of the Bene-Ammon dies, and Hanun his son reigns in his stead,
10.2: and David says, `I do kindness with Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did with me kindness;' and David sends to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father, and the servants of David come in to the land of the Bene-Ammon.
10.3: And the heads of the Bene-Ammon say to Hanun their lord, `Is David honouring your father in your eyes because he has sent to you comforters? for to search the city, and to spy it, and to overthrow it, has not David sent his servants to you?'
10.4: And Hanun takes the servants of David, and shaves off the half of their beard, and cuts off their long robes in the midst--to their buttocks, and sends them away;
10.5: and they declare it to David, and he sends to meet them, for the men have been greatly ashamed, and the king says, `Abide in Jericho till your beard does spring up--then you have returned.'
10.6: And the Bene-Ammon see that they have been abhorred by David, and the Bene-Ammon send and hire Aram of Beth-Rehob, and Aram of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and Ish-Tob with twelve thousand men;
10.7: and David hears, and sends Joab, and all the host--the mighty men.
10.8: And the Bene-Ammon come out, and set battle in array, at the opening of the gate, and Aram of Zoba, and Rehob, and Ish-Tob, and Maacah, are by themselves in the field;
10.9: and Joab sees that the front of the battle has been to him before and behind, and he chooses of all the chosen in Israel, and sets in array to meet Aram,
10.10: and the rest of the people he has given into the hand of Abishai his brother, and sets in array to meet the Bene-Ammon.
10.11: And he says, `If Aram be stronger than I, then you have been to me for salvation, and if the Bene-Ammon be stronger than you, then I have come to give salvation to you;
10.12: be strong and strengthen yourself for our people, and for the cities of our God, and Jehovah does that which is good in His eyes.'
10.13: And Joab draws nigh, and the people who are with him, to battle against Aram, and they flee from his presence;
10.14: and the Bene-Ammon have seen that Aram has fled, and they flee from the presence of Abishai, and go in to the city; and Joab turns back from the Bene-Ammon, and comes in to Jerusalem.
10.15: And Aram sees that it is smitten before Israel, and they are gathered together;
10.16: and Hadadezer sends, and brings out Aram which is beyond the River, and they come in to Helam, and Shobach head of the host of Hadadezer is before them.
10.17: And it is declared to David, and he gathers all Israel, and passes over the Jordan, and comes in to Helam, and Aram sets itself in array to meet David, and they fight with him;
10.18: and Aram flees from the presence of Israel, and David slays of Aram seven hundred charioteers, and forty thousand horsemen, and Shobach head of its host he has smitten, and he dies there.
10.19: And all the kings--servants of Hadadezer--see that they have been smitten before Israel, and make peace with Israel, and serve them; and Aram is afraid to help any more the Bene-Ammon.

11.1: And it comes to pass, at the revolution of the year--at the time of the going out of the messengers--that David sends Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel, and they destroy the Bene-Ammon, and lay siege against Rabbah. And David is dwelling in Jerusalem,
11.2: and it comes to pass, at evening-time, that David rises from off his couch, and walks up and down on the roof of the king's house, and sees from the roof a woman bathing, and the woman is of very good appearance,
11.3: and David sends and inquires about the woman, and says, `Is not this Bath-Sheba, daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite?'
11.4: And David sends messengers, and takes her, and she comes to him, and he lies with her--and she is purifying herself from her uncleanness--and she turns back to her house;
11.5: and the woman conceives, and sends, and declares to David, and says, `I am conceiving.'
11.6: And David sends to Joab, `Send to me Uriah the Hittite,' and Joab sends Uriah to David;
11.7: and Uriah comes to him, and David asks of the prosperity of Joab, and of the prosperity of the people, and of the prosperity of the war.
11.8: And David says to Uriah, `Go down to your house, and wash your feet;' and Uriah goes out of the king's house, and there goes out after him a gift from the king,
11.9: and Uriah lies down at the opening of the king's house, with all the servants of his lord, and has not gone down to his house.
11.10: And they declare to David, saying, `Uriah has not gone down to his house;' and David says to Uriah, `Have you not come from a journey? wherefore have you not gone down to your house?'
11.11: And Uriah says to David, `The ark, and Israel, and Judah, are abiding in booths, and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, on the face of the field are encamping; and I--I go in to my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife! --your life, and the life of your soul--if I do this thing.'
11.12: And David says to Uriah, `Abide in this place also to-day, and to-morrow I send you away;' and Uriah abides in Jerusalem, on that day, and on the morrow,
11.13: and David calls for him, and he eats before him, and drinks, and he causes him to drink, and he goes out in the evening to lie on his couch with the servants of his lord, and to his house he has not gone down.
11.14: And it comes to pass in the morning, that David writes a letter to Joab, and sends by the hand of Uriah;
11.15: and he writes in the letter, saying, `Place you Uriah over-against the front of the sever battle, and you have turned back from after him, and he has been smitten, and has died.'
11.16: And it comes to pass in Joab's watching of the city, that he appoints Uriah to the place where he knew that valiant men are;
11.17: and the men of the city go out and fight with Joab, and there fall some of the people, of the servants of David; and there dies also Uriah the Hittite.
11.18: And Joab sends and declares to David all the matters of the war,
11.19: and commands the messenger, saying, `At your finishing all the matters of the war to speak to the king,
11.20: then, it has been, if the king's fury ascend, and he has said to you, Wherefore did you draw nigh to the city to fight? did you not know that they shoot from off the wall?
11.21: Who smote Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast on him a piece of a rider from the wall, and he dies in Thebez? why drew you nigh to the wall? that you have said, Also your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.'
11.22: And the messenger goes, and comes in, and declares to David all that with which Joab sent him,
11.23: and the messenger says to David, `Surely the men have been mighty against us, and come out to us into the field, and we are upon them to the opening of the gate,
11.24: and those shooting shoot at your servants from off the wall, and some of the servants of the king are dead, and also, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead.
11.25: And David says to the messenger, `Thus do you say to Joab, Let not this thing be evil in your eyes; for thus and thus does the sword devour; strengthen your warfare against the city, and throw it down--and strengthen you him.'
11.26: And the wife of Uriah hears that Uriah her husband is dead, and laments for her lord;
11.27: and the mourning passes by, and David sends and gathers her to his house, and she is to him for a wife, and bears to him a son; and the thing which David has done is evil in the eyes of Jehovah.

12.1: And Jehovah sends Nathan to David, and he comes to him, and says to him: `Two men have been in one city; One rich and one poor;
12.2: The rich has flocks and herds very many;
12.3: And the poor one has nothing, Except one little ewe-lamb, Which he has bought, and keeps alive, And it grows up with him, And with his sons together; Of his morsel it eats, And from his cup it drinks, And in his bosom it lies, And it is to him as a daughter;
12.4: And there comes a traveller to the rich man, And he spares to take Of his own flock, and of his own herd, To prepare for the traveller Who has come to him, And he takes the ewe-lamb of the poor man, And prepares it for the man Who has come to him.'
12.5: And the anger of David burns against the man exceedingly, and he says to Nathan, `Jehovah lives, surely a son of death is the man who is doing this,
12.6: and the ewe-lamb he does repay fourfold, because that he has done this thing, and because that he had no pity.'
12.7: And Nathan says to David, `You are the man! Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, I anointed you for king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul;
12.8: and I give to you the house of your lord, and the wives of your lord, into your bosom, and I give to you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if little, then I add to you such and such things.
12.9: `Wherefore have you despised the word of Jehovah, to do the evil thing in His eyes? Uriah the Hittite you have smitten by the sword, and his wife you have taken to you for a wife, and him you have slain by the sword of the Bene-Ammon.
12.10: `And now, the sword does not turn aside from your house to the age, because you have despised Me, and do take the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be to you for a wife;
12.11: thus said Jehovah, Indeed, I am raising up against you evil, out of your house, and have taken your wives before your eyes, and given to your neighbour, and he has lain with your wives before the eyes of this sun;
12.12: for you have done it in secret, and I do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.'
12.13: And David says to Nathan, `I have sinned against Jehovah.' And Nathan says to David, `Also--Jehovah has caused your sin to pass away; you do not die;
12.14: only, because you have caused the enemies of Jehovah greatly to despise by this thing, also the son who is born to you does surely die.'
12.15: And Nathan goes to his house, and Jehovah smites the lad, whom the wife of Uriah has born to David, and it is incurable;
12.16: and David seeks God for the youth, and David keeps a fast, and has gone in and lodged, and lain on the earth.
12.17: And the elders of his house rise against him, to raise him up from the earth, and he has not been willing, nor has he eaten with them bread;
12.18: and it comes to pass on the seventh day, that the lad dies, and the servants of David fear to declare to him that the lad is dead, for they said, `Indeed, in the lad being alive we spoke to him, and he did not hearken to our voice; and how do we say to him, The lad is dead? --then he has done evil.'
12.19: And David sees that his servants are whispering, and David understands that the lad is dead, and David says to his servants, `Is the lad dead?' and they say, `Dead.'
12.20: And David rises from the earth, and does bathe and anoint himself, and changes his raiment, and comes in to the house of Jehovah, and bows himself, and comes to his house, and asks and they place for him bread, and he eats.
12.21: And his servants say to him, `What is this thing you have done? because of the living lad you have fasted and do weep, and when the lad is dead you have risen and do eat bread.'
12.22: And he says, `While the lad is alive I have fasted, and weep, for I said, Who knows? --Jehovah does pity me, and the lad has lived;
12.23: and now, he has died, why is this--I fast? am I able to bring him back again? I am going to him, and he does not turn back to me.'
12.24: And David comforts Bath-Sheba his wife, and goes in to her, and lies with her, and she bears a son, and he calls his name Solomon; and Jehovah has loved him,
12.25: and sends by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and calls his name Jedidiah, because of Jehovah.
12.26: And Joab fights against Rabbah of the Bene-Ammon, and captures the royal city,
12.27: and Joab sends messengers to David, and says, `I have fought against Rabbah--also I have captured the city of waters;
12.28: and now, gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city, and capture it, lest I capture the city, and my name has been called upon it.'
12.29: And David gathers all the people, and goes to Rabbah, and fights against it, and captures it;
12.30: and he takes the crown of their king from off his head, and its weight is a talent of gold, and precious stones, and it is on the head of David; and the spoil of the city he has brought out, very much;
12.31: and the people who are in it he has brought out, and sets to the saw, and to cutting instruments of iron, and to axes of iron, and has caused them to pass over into the brick-kiln; and so he does to all the cities of the Bene-Ammon; and David turns back, and all the people, to Jerusalem.

13.1: And it comes to pass afterwards that Absalom son of David has a fair sister, and her name is Tamar, and Amnon son of David loves her.
13.2: And Amnon has distress--even to become sick, because of Tamar his sister, for she is a virgin, and it is hard in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.
13.3: And Amnon has a friend, and his name is Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother, and Jonadab is a very wise man,
13.4: and says to him, `Wherefore are you thus lean, O king's son, morning by morning? do you not declare to me?' And Amnon says to him, `Tamar--sister of Absalom my brother--I am loving.'
13.5: And Jonadab says to him, `Lie down on your couch, and feign yourself sick, and your father has come in to see you, and you have said to him, `Let, I pray you, Tamar my sister come in and give me bread to eat; and she has made the food before my eyes so that I see it, and have eaten from her hand.'
13.6: And Amnon lies down, and feigns himself sick, and the king comes in to see him, and Amnon says to the king, `Let, I pray you, Tamar my sister come, and she makes before my eyes two cakes, and I eat from her hand.'
13.7: And David sends to Tamar, to the house, saying, `Go, I pray you, to the house of Amnon your brother, and make for him food.'
13.8: And Tamar goes to the house of Amnon her brother, and he is lying down, and she takes the dough, and kneads, and makes cakes before his eyes, and cooks the cakes,
13.9: and takes the frying-pan, and pours out before him, and he refuses to eat, and Amnon says, `Take you out every one from me;' and they go out every one from him.
13.10: And Amnon says to Tamar, `Bring the food into the inner chamber, and I eat from your hand;' and Tamar takes the cakes that she has made, and brings in to Amnon her brother, into the inner chamber,
13.11: and she brings nigh to him to eat, and he lays hold on her, and says to her, `Come, lie with me, my sister.'
13.12: And she says to him, `No, my brother, do not humble me, for it is not done so in Israel; do not this folly.
13.13: And I--where do I cause my reproach to go? and you--you are as one of the fools in Israel; and now, speak, I pray you, to the king; for he does not withhold me from you.'
13.14: And he has not been willing to hearken to her voice, and is stronger than she, and humbles her, and lies with her.
13.15: And Amnon hates her--a very great hatred--that greater is the hatred with which he has hated her than the love with which he loved her, and Amnon says to her, `Rise, go.'
13.16: And she says to him, `Because of the circumstances this evil is greater than the other that you have done with me--to send me away;' and he has not been willing to hearken to her,
13.17: and calls his young man, his servant, and says, `Send away, I pray you, this one from me without, and bolt the door after her;'
13.18: --and upon her is a long coat, for such upper robes do daughters of the king who are virgins put on, --and his servant takes her out without, and has bolted the door after her.
13.19: And Tamar takes ashes for her head, and the long coat that is on her she has rent, and puts her hand on her head, and goes, going on and crying;
13.20: and Absalom her brother says to her, `Has Amnon your brother been with you? and now, my sister, keep silent, he is your brother; set not your heart to this thing;' and Tamar dwells--but desolate--in the house of Absalom her brother.
13.21: And king David has heard all these things, and it is very displeasing to him;
13.22: and Absalom has not spoken with Amnon either evil or good, for Absalom is hating Amnon, because that he humbled Tamar his sister.
13.23: And it comes to pass, after two years of days, that Absalom has shearers in Baal-Hazor, which is with Ephraim, and Absalom calls for all the sons of the king.
13.24: And Absalom comes to the king, and says, `Indeed, I pray you, your servant has shearers, let the king go, I pray you, and his servants, with your servant.'
13.25: And the king says to Absalom, `No, my son, let us not all go, I pray you, and we are not too heavy on you;' and he presses on him, and he has not been willing to go, and he blesses him.
13.26: And Absalom says, `If not--let, I pray you, Amnon my brother go with us;' and the king says to him, `Why does he go with you?'
13.27: and Absalom urges on him, and he sends with him Amnon, and all the sons of the king.
13.28: And Absalom commands his young men, saying, `See, I pray you, when the heart of Amnon is glad with wine, and I have said to you, Smite Amnon, that you have put him to death; fear not; is it not because I have commanded you? be strong, yes, become sons of valour.'
13.29: And the young men of Absalom do to Amnon as Absalom commanded, and rise do all the sons of the king, and they ride, each on his mule, and flee.
13.30: And it comes to pass--they are in the way--and the report has come to David, saying, `Absalom has smitten all the sons of the king, and there is not left of them one;'
13.31: and the king rises, and rends his garments, and lies on the earth, and all his servants are standing by with rent garments.
13.32: And Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, answers and says, `Let not my lord say, The whole of the young men, the sons of the king, they have put to death; for Amnon alone is dead, for by the command of Absalom it has been appointed from the day of his humbling Tamar his sister;
13.33: and now, let not my lord the king lay to his heart the word, saying, All the sons of the king have died, for Amnon alone is dead.'
13.34: And Absalom flees, and the young man who is watching lifts up his eyes and looks, and indeed, much people are coming by the way behind him, on the side of the hill.
13.35: And Jonadab says to the king, `Indeed, the sons of the king have come; as the word of your servant, so it has been.'
13.36: And it comes to pass at his finishing to speak, that indeed, the sons of the king have come, and they lift up their voice, and weep, and also the king and all his servants have wept--a very great weeping.
13.37: And Absalom has fled, and goes to Talmai, son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, and David mourns for his son all the days.
13.38: And Absalom has fled, and goes to Geshur, and is there three years;
13.39: and the soul of king David determines to go out to Absalom, for he has been comforted for Amnon, for he is dead.

14.1: And Joab son of Zeruial knows that the heart of the king is on Absalom,
14.2: and Joab sends to Tekoah, and takes from there a wise woman, and says to her, `Feign yourself a mourner, I pray you, and put on, I pray you, garments of mourning, and anoint not yourself with oil, and you have been as a woman these many days mourning for the dead,
14.3: and you have gone to the king, and spoken to him, according to this word;' and Joab puts the words into her mouth.
14.4: And the woman of Tekoah speaks to the king, and falls on her face to the earth, and does obeisance, and says, `Save, O king.'
14.5: And the king says to her, `What--to you?' and she says, `Truly a widow woman am I, and my husband dies,
14.6: and your maid-servant has two sons; and they strive both of them in a field, and there is no deliverer between them, and the one smites the other, and puts him to death;
14.7: and indeed, the whole family has risen against your maid-servant, and say, Give up him who smites his brother, and we put him to death for the life of his brother whom he has slain, and we destroy also the heir; and they have quenched my coal which is left--so as not to set to my husband a name and remnant on the face of the ground.'
14.8: And the king says to the woman, `Go to your house, and I give charge concerning you.'
14.9: And the woman of Tekoah says to the king, `On me, my lord, O king, is the iniquity, and on the house of my father; and the king and his throne are innocent.'
14.10: And the king says, `He who speaks anything to you, and you have brought him to me, then he does not add any more to come against you.'
14.11: And she says, `Let, I pray you, the king remember by Jehovah your God, that the redeemer of blood add not to destroy, and they destroy not my son;' and he says, `Jehovah lives; if there does fall of the hair of your son to the earth.'
14.12: And the woman says, `Let, I pray you, your maid-servant speak to my lord the king a word;' and he says, `Speak.'
14.13: And the woman says, `And why have you thought thus concerning the people of God? yes, the king is speaking this thing as a guilty one, in that the king has not brought back his outcast;
14.14: for we do surely die, and are as water which is running down to the earth, which is not gathered, and God does not accept a person, and has devised devices in that the outcast is not outcast by Him.
14.15: `And now that I have come to speak to the king my lord this word, it is because the people made me afraid, and your maid-servant says, Let me speak, I pray you, to the king; it may be the king does do the word of his handmaid,
14.16: for the king does hearken to deliver his handmaid out of the paw of the man seeking to destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God,
14.17: and your maid-servant says, Let, I pray you, the word of my lord the king be for ease; for as a messenger of God so is my lord the king, to understand the good and the evil; and Jehovah your God is with you.'
14.18: And the king answers and says to the woman, `Do not, I pray you, hide from me the thing that I am asking you;' and the woman says, `Let, I pray you, my lord the king speak.'
14.19: And the king says, `Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?' And the woman answers and says, `Your soul lives, my lord, O king, none does turn to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab he commanded me, and he put in the mouth of your maid-servant all these words;
14.20: in order to bring round the appearance of the thing has your servant Joab done this thing, and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of a messenger of God, to know all that is in the land.'
14.21: And the king says to Joab, `Indeed, I pray you, you have done this thing; and go, bring back the young man Absalom.'
14.22: And Joab falls on his face to the earth, and does obeisance, and blesses the king, and Joab says, `To-day has your servant known that I have found grace in your eyes, my lord, O king, in that the king has done the word of his servant.'
14.23: And Joab rises and goes to Geshur, and brings in Absalom to Jerusalem,
14.24: and the king says, `Let him turn round to his house, and my face he does not see.' And Absalom turns round to his house, and the face of the king he has not seen.
14.25: And like Absalom there was no man so fair in all Israel, to praise greatly; from the sole of his foot even to his crown there was no blemish in him;
14.26: and in his polling his head--and it has been at the end of year by year that he polls it, for it is heavy on him, and he has polled it--he has even weighed out the hair of his head--two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
14.27: And there are born to Absalom three sons, and one daughter, and her name is Tamar; she was a woman of a fair appearance.
14.28: And Absalom dwells in Jerusalem two years of days, and the face of the king he has not seen;
14.29: and Absalom sends to Joab, to send him to the king, and he has not been willing to come to him; and he sends again a second time, and he has not been willing to come.
14.30: And he says to his servants, `See, the portion of Joab is by the side of mine, and he has barley there; go, and burn it with fire;' and the servants of Absalom burn the portion with fire.
14.31: And Joab rises and comes to Absalom in the house, and says to him, `Why have your servants burned the portion that I have with fire?'
14.32: And Absalom says to Joab, `Indeed, I sent to you, saying, Come here, and I send you to the king to say, Why have I come in from Geshur? --good for me while I am there--and now, let me see the king's face, and if there is in me iniquity then you have put me to death.'
14.33: And Joab comes to the king, and declares it to him, and he calls to Absalom, and he comes to the king, and bows himself to him, on his face, to the earth, before the king, and the king gives a kiss to Absalom.

15.1: And it comes to pass afterwards, that Absalom prepares for himself a chariot, and horses, and fifty men are running before him;
15.2: and Absalom has risen early, and stood by the side of the way of the gate, and it comes to pass, every man who has a pleading to come to the king for judgment, that Absalom calls to him, and says, `Of what city are you?' and he says, `Of one of the tribes of Israel is your servant.'
15.3: And Absalom says to him, `See, your matters are good and straightforward--and there is none hearkening to you from the king.'
15.4: And Absalom says, `Who does make me a judge in the land, that to me does come every man who has a plea and judgment? --then I have declared him righteous.'
15.5: And it has come to pass, in the drawing nearing of any one to bow himself to him, that he has put forth his hand, and laid hold on him, and given a kiss to him;
15.6: and Absalom does according to this thing to all Israel who come in for judgment to the king, and Absalom steals the heart of the men of Israel.
15.7: And it comes to pass, at the end of forty years, that Absalom says to the king, `Let me go, I pray you, and I complete my vow, that I vowed to Jehovah in Hebron,
15.8: for a vow has your servant vowed in my dwelling in Geshur, in Aram, saying, If Jehovah does certainly bring me back to Jerusalem, then I have served Jehovah.'
15.9: And the king says to him, `Go in peace;' and he rises and goes to Hebron,
15.10: and Absalom sends spies through all the tribes of Israel, saying, `At your hearing the voice of the trumpet, then you have said, Absalom has reigned in Hebron.'
15.11: And with Absalom have gone two hundred men, out of Jerusalem, invited ones, and they are going in their simplicity, and have not known anything;
15.12: and Absalom sends Ahithophel the Gilonite, a counsellor of David, out of his city, out of Gilo, in his sacrificing sacrifices; and the conspiracy is strong, and the people are going and increasing with Absalom.
15.13: And he who is declaring tidings comes in to David, saying, `The heart of the men of Israel has been after Absalom.'
15.14: And David says to all his servants who are with him in Jerusalem, `Rise, and we flee, for we have no escape from the face of Absalom; haste to go, lest he hasten, and have overtaken us, and forced on us evil, and smitten the city by the mouth of the sword.'
15.15: And the servants of the king say to the king, `According to all that my lord the king chooses--indeed, your servants do.'
15.16: And the king goes out, and all his household at his feet, and the king leaves ten women--concubines--to keep the house.
15.17: And the king goes out, and all the people at his feet, and they stand still at the farthest off house.
15.18: And all his servants are passing on at his side, and all the Cherethite, and all the Pelethite, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came at his feet from Gath, are passing on at the front of the king.
15.19: And the king says to Ittai the Gittite, `Why do you go--you also--with us? turn back--and abide with the king, for you are a stranger, and also an exile you--to your place.
15.20: Yesterday is your coming in, and to-day I move you to go with us, and I am going on that which I am going! --turn back, and take back your brethren with you, --kindness and truth.'
15.21: And Ittai answers the king and says, `Jehovah lives, and my lord the king lives, surely in the place where my lord the king is--if for death, if for life, surely there is your servant.'
15.22: And David says to Ittai, `Go and pass over;' and Ittai the Gittite passes over, and all his men, and all the infants who are with him.
15.23: And all the land are weeping--a great voice, and all the people are passing over; and the king is passing over through the brook Kidron, and all the people are passing over on the front of the way of the wilderness;
15.24: and indeed, also Zadok, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God, and they make the ark of God firm, and Abiathar goes up, till the completion of all the people to pass over out of the city.
15.25: And the king says to Zadok, `Take back the ark of God to the city; if I find grace in the eyes of Jehovah, then He has brought me back, and shown me it and His habitation;
15.26: and if thus He say, I have not delighted in you; here am I, He does to me as is good in His eyes.'
15.27: And the king says to Zadok the priest, `Are you a seer? turn back to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons with you;
15.28: see you, I am tarrying in the plains of the wilderness till the coming in of a word from you to declare to me.'
15.29: And Zadok takes back--and Abiathar--the ark of God to Jerusalem, and they abide there.
15.30: And David is going up in the ascent of the olives, going up and weeping, and he has the head covered, and he is going barefooted, and all the people who are with him have covered each his head, and have gone up, going up and weeping;
15.31: and David declared, saying, `Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom;' and David says, `Make foolish, I pray You, the counsel of Ahithophel, O Jehovah.'
15.32: And it comes to pass, David has come to the top, where he bows himself to God, and indeed, to meet him is Hushai the Archite, his coat rent, and earth on his head;
15.33: and David says to him, `If you have passed on with me then you have been on me for a burden,
15.34: and if to the city you do turn back, and have said to Absalom, Your servant I am, O king; servant of your father I am also hitherto, and now, I am also your servant; then you have made void for me the counsel of Ahithophel;
15.35: and are there not with you there Zadok and Abiathar the priests? and it has been, the whole of the matter that you hear from the house of the king you do declare to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests.
15.36: Indeed, there with them are their two sons, Ahimaaz to Zadok, and Jonathan to Abiathar, and you have sent by their hand to me anything that you hear.'
15.37: And Hushai, David's friend, comes in to the city, and Absalom comes in to Jerusalem.

16.1: And David has passed on a little from the top, and indeed, Ziba, servant of Mephibosheth--to meet him, and a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and a hundred of summer-fruit, and a bottle of wine.
16.2: And the king says to Ziba, `What--these to you?' and Ziba says, `The asses for the household of the king to ride on, and the bread and the summer-fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for the wearied to drink in the wilderness.'
16.3: And the king says, `And where is the son of your lord?' and Ziba says to the king, `Indeed, he is abiding in Jerusalem, for he said, To-day do the house of Israel give back to me the kingdom of my father.'
16.4: And the king says to Ziba, `Indeed, yours are all that Mephibosheth has;' and Ziba says, `I have bowed myself--I find grace in your eyes, my lord, O king.'
16.5: And king David has come in to Bahurim, and indeed, from there a man is coming out, of the family of the house of Saul, and his name is Shimei, son of Gera, he comes out, coming out and reviling;
16.6: and he stones David with stones, and all the servants of king David, and all the people, and all the mighty men on his right and on his left.
16.7: And thus said Shimei in his reviling, `Go out, go out, O man of blood, and man of worthlessness!
16.8: Jehovah has turned back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead you have reigned, and Jehovah does give the kingdom in to the hand of Absalom your son; and indeed, you are in your evil, for a man of blood you are.'
16.9: And Abishai son of Zeruiah says to the king, `Why does this dead dog revile my lord the king? let me pass over, I pray you, and I turn aside his head.'
16.10: And the king says, `What--to me and to you, O sons of Zeruiah? for--let him revile; even because Jehovah has said to him, Revile David; and who says, Wherefore have You done so?'
16.11: And David says to Abishai, and to all his servants, `Indeed, my son who came out of my bowels is seeking my life, and also surely now the Benjamite; leave him alone, and let him revile, for Jehovah has said so to him;
16.12: it may be Jehovah does look on my affliction, and Jehovah has turned back to me good for his reviling this day.'
16.13: And David goes with his men in the way, and Shimei is going at the side of the hill over-against him, going on, and he reviles, and stones with stones over-against him, and has dusted with dust.
16.14: And the king comes in, and all the people who are with him, wearied, and they are refreshed there.
16.15: And Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, have come in to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him,
16.16: and it comes to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, has come to Absalom, that Hushai says to Absalom, `Let the king live! let the king live!'
16.17: And Absalom says to Hushai, `This your kindness with your friend! why have you not gone with your friend?'
16.18: And Hushai says to Absalom, `No, for he whom Jehovah has chosen, and this people, even all the men of Israel, his I am, and with him I abide;
16.19: and secondly, for whom do I labour? is it not before his son? as I served before your father so am I before you.'
16.20: And Absalom says to Ahithophel, `Give for you counsel what we do.'
16.21: And Ahithophel says to Absalom, `Go in to the concubines of your father, whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel has heard that you have been abhorred by your father, and the hands of all who are with you have been strong.'
16.22: And they spread out for Absalom the tent on the roof, and Absalom goes in to the concubines of his father before the eyes of all Israel.
16.23: And the counsel of Ahithophel which he counselled in those days is as when one inquires at the word of God; so is all the counsel of Ahithophel both to David and to Absalom.

17.1: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, `Let me choose, I pray you, twelve thousand men, and I arise and pursue after David to-night,
17.2: and come upon him, and he weary and feeble-handed, and I have caused him to tremble, and all the people have fled who are with him, and I have smitten the king by himself,
17.3: and I bring back all the people to you--as the turning back of the whole is the man whom you are seeking--all the people are peace.
17.4: And the thing is right in the eyes of Absalom, and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
17.5: And Absalom says, `Call, I pray you, also for Hushai the Archite, and we hear what is in his mouth--even he.'
17.6: And Hushai comes in to Absalom, and Absalom speaks to him, saying, `According to this word has Ahithophel spoken; do we do his word? if not, you--speak you.'
17.7: And Hushai says to Absalom, `Not good is the counsel that Ahithophel has counselled at this time.'
17.8: And Hushai says, `You have known your father and his men, that they are heroes, and they are bitter in soul as a bereaved bear in a field, and your father is a man of war, and does not lodge with the people;
17.9: indeed, now, he is hidden in one of the pits, or in one of the places, and it has been, at the falling among them at the commencement, that the hearer has heard, and said, There has been a slaughter among the people who are after Absalom;
17.10: and he also, the son of valour, whose heart is as the heart of the lion, does utterly melt, for all Israel does know that your father is a hero, and sons of valour are those with him.
17.11: `So that I have counselled: Let all Israel be diligently gathered to you, from Dan even to Beer-Sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude, and you yourself are going in the midst;
17.12: and we have come in to him in one of the places where he is found, and we are upon him as the dew falls on the ground, and there has not been left of him and of all the men who are with him even one.
17.13: And if to a city he is gathered, then they have caused all Israel to bear to that city ropes, and we have drawn it to the brook till that there has not been found there even a stone.'
17.14: And Absalom says--and all the men of Israel--`Better is the counsel of Hushai the Archite than the counsel of Ahithophel;' and Jehovah willed to make void the good counsel of Ahithophel for the sake of Jehovah's bringing to Absalom the evil.
17.15: And Hushai says to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, `Thus and thus has Ahithophel counselled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I have counselled;
17.16: and now, send hastily, and declare to David, saying, Lodge not to-night in the plains of the wilderness, and also, certainly pass over, lest there be a swallowing up of the king and of all the people who are with him.'
17.17: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz are standing at En-Rogel, and the maid-servant has gone and declared to them--and they go and have declared it to king David--for they are not able to be seen to go in to the city.
17.18: And a youth sees them, and declares to Absalom; and they go on both of them hastily, and come in to the house of a man in Bahurim, and he has a well in his court, and they go down there,
17.19: and the woman takes and spreads the covering over the face of the well, and spreads on it the ground corn, and the thing has not been known.
17.20: And the servants of Absalom come in to the woman to the house, and say, `Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?' and the woman says to them, `They passed over the brook of water;' and they seek, and have not found, and turn back to Jerusalem.
17.21: And it comes to pass, after their going on, that they come up out of the well, and go and declare to king David, and say to David, `Rise you, and pass over hastily the waters, for thus has Ahithophel counselled against you.'
17.22: And David rises, and all the people who are with him, and they pass over the Jordan, till the light of the morning, till one has not been lacking who has not passed over the Jordan.
17.23: And Ahithophel has seen that his counsel was not done, and he saddles the ass, and rises and goes to his house, to his city, and gives charge to his household, and strangles himself, and dies, and he is buried in the burying-place of his father.
17.24: And David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him;
17.25: and Amasa has Absalom set instead of Joab over the host, and Amasa is a man's son whose name is Ithra the Israelite who has gone in to Abigail, daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab;
17.26: and Israel encamps with Absalom in the land of Gilead.
17.27: And it comes to pass at the coming in of David to Mahanaim, that Shobi, son of Nahash, from Rabbah of the Bene-Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel, from Indeed-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite, from Rogelim,
17.28: couch, and basin, and earthen vessel, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and roasted corn, and beans, and lentiles, and roasted pulse,
17.29: and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, have brought nigh for David, and for the people who are with him to eat, for they said, `Your people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.'

18.1: And David inspects the people who are with him, and sets over them heads of thousands and heads of hundreds,
18.2: and David sends the third of the people by the hand of Joab, and the third by the hand of Abishai, son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and the third by the hand of Ittai the Gittite, and the king says to the people, `I certainly go out--I also--with you.'
18.3: And the people say, `You do not go out, for if we utterly flee, they do not set their heart upon us; and if half of us die, they do not set their heart to us--for now like us are ten thousand; and now, better that you be to us from the city for an helper.'
18.4: And the king says to them, `That which is good in your eyes I do;' and the king stands at the side of the gate, and all the people have gone out by hundreds and by thousands,
18.5: and the king charges Joab, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying, `Gently--for me, for the youth, for Absalom;' and all the people heard in the king's charging all the heads concerning Absalom.
18.6: And the people goes out into the field to meet Israel, and the battle is in a forest of Ephraim;
18.7: and smitten there are the people of Israel before the servants of David, and the smiting there is great on that day--twenty thousand;
18.8: and the battle is there scattered over the face of all the land, and the forest multiplies to devour among the people more than those whom the sword has devoured in that day.
18.9: And Absalom meets before the servants of David, and Absalom is riding on the mule, and the mule comes in under an entangled bough of the great oak, and his head takes hold on the oak, and he is placed between the heavens and the earth, and the mule that is under him has passed on.
18.10: And one man sees, and declares to Joab, and says, `Indeed, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.'
18.11: And Joab says to the man who is declaring it to him, `And indeed, you have seen--and wherefore did you not smite him there to the earth--and on me to give to you ten silverlings and one girdle?'
18.12: And the man says to Joab, `Yes, though I am weighing on my hand a thousand silverlings, I do not put forth my hand to the son of the king; for in our ears has the king charged you, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying, Observe you who is against the youth--against Absalom;
18.13: or I had done against my soul a vain thing, and no matter is hid from the king, and you--you do station yourself over-against.'
18.14: And Joab says, `Not right--I tarry before you;' and he takes three darts in his hand, and strikes them into the heart of Absalom, while he is alive, in the midst of the oak.
18.15: And they go round--ten youths bearing weapons of Joab--and smite Absalom, and put him to death.
18.16: And Joab blows with a trumpet, and the people turns back from pursuing after Israel, for Joab has kept back the people;
18.17: and they take Absalom and cast him in the forest to the great pit, and set up over him a very great heap of stones, and all Israel have fled--each to his tent.
18.18: And Absalom has taken, and sets up for himself in his life, the standing-pillar that is in the king's valley, for he said, `I have no son to cause my name to be remembered;' and he calls the standing-pillar by his own name, and it is called `The monument of Absalom' to this day.
18.19: And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, `Let me run, I pray you, and I bear the king tidings, for Jehovah has delivered him out of the hand of his enemies;'
18.20: and Joab says to him, `You are not a man of tidings this day, but you have borne tidings on another day, and this day you do not bear tidings, because the king's son is dead.'
18.21: And Joab says to Cushi, `Go, declare to the king that which you have seen;' and Cushi bows himself to Joab, and runs.
18.22: And Ahimaaz son of Zadok adds again, and says to Joab, `And whatever it be, let me run, I pray you, I also, after the Cushite.' And Joab says, `Why is this--you are running, my son, and for you there are no tidings found?' --
18.23: `And, whatever it be, said he, let me run.' And he says to him, `Run;' and Ahimaaz runs the way of the circuit, and passes by the Cushite.
18.24: And David is sitting between the two gates, and the watchman goes to the roof of the gate, to the wall, and lifts up his eyes, and looks, and indeed, a man running by himself.
18.25: And the watchman calls, and declares to the king, and the king says, `If by himself, tidings are in his mouth;' and he comes, coming on and drawing near.
18.26: And the watchman sees another man running, and the watchman calls to the gatekeeper, and says, `Indeed, a man running by himself;' and the king says, `Also this one is bearing tidings.'
18.27: And the watchman says, `I see the running of the first as the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok.' And the king says, `This is a good man, and with good tidings he comes.'
18.28: And Ahimaaz calls and says to the king, `Peace;' and he bows himself to the king, on his face, to the earth, and says, `Blessed is Jehovah your God who has shut up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king.'
18.29: And the king says, `Peace to the youth--to Absalom?' And Ahimaaz says, `I saw the great multitude, at the sending away of the servant of the king, even your servant by Joab, and I have not known what it is.'
18.30: And the king says, `Turn round, station yourself here;' and he turns round and stands still.
18.31: And indeed, the Cushite has come, and the Cushite says, `Let tidings be proclaimed, my lord, O king; for Jehovah has delivered you to-day out of the hand of all those rising up against you.'
